general_background.title: Phosphines and precursor solutions
general_background.summary: Elemental selenium can react with organophosphines to form soluble phosphorus-selenium-containing precursor species. Organic substituents can make these species compatible with an organic medium, while their composition and reactivity depend on the phosphine and preparation conditions.

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
